<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `gen.sh` is a PKGBUILD generator that automates the creation of a package build script for an AUR package. It takes a version number as input, queries the GitHub API for release assets with a `.tar` extension, and dynamically constructs a PKGBUILD file based on those assets. The script uses standard and expected tools like `curl` and `jq` to interact with the GitHub API, which is common in AUR helper scripts.

It downloads source files from the project's own GitHub release page (`https://github.com/ahmedmoselhi/distro-grub-themes`), constructs a valid PKGBUILD with appropriate metadata, and runs `updpkgsums` to update checksums. These behaviors are consistent with standard AUR maintainer workflows. While the `md5sums` array is initially set to a placeholder value `(123)`, this is immediately followed by a call to `updpkgsums`, which will overwrite it with correct values—this is a normal pattern in dynamic PKGBUILD generation.

There is no evidence of malicious behavior such as exfiltration of system data, execution of remote code, obfuscation, or unauthorized network requests. The script operates transparently and generates a package definition that reflects the actual upstream release assets. All actions are confined to package metadata generation and are part of legitimate AUR maintenance practices.
</details>
